name: Jina Reader
summary: Jina Reader is a free API that turns any web page into clean Markdown for AI models just by putting r.jina.ai in front of the URL.

free_plan_covers.note: No account needed: 20 requests a minute with no monthly cap; a free API key raises that to 500 requests a minute plus 10 million free tokens to spend.

first_paid_usd_month.note: No fixed monthly plan; usage beyond the free tokens is pay-as-you-go by token, topped up as needed.

portability.note: It's a plain HTTP request with the target URL appended to r.jina.ai, no SDK or account required, so switching to another reader or markdown service later is a small change.

scraper_runs.note: You request https://r.jina.ai/ followed by the page's URL, and Jina's servers fetch and render the page and hand back Markdown.

js_rendering.note: The default engine renders the page in a headless browser before extracting it, at no extra cost over the standard token pricing.

ai_ready_output.note: Turning pages into clean, LLM-ready Markdown is Reader's whole purpose.

price_per_1k_pages.note: Could not verify: Reader draws from the same prepaid token wallet as Jina's other AI APIs, and the exact per-token dollar rate only shows up after logging into the dashboard, so an accurate cost per 1,000 pages beyond the 10 million free tokens couldn't be confirmed from public docs.

setup.step: No account is required for basic use; call the Reader endpoint directly by putting r.jina.ai/ in front of any URL.
For higher rate limits, create a free Jina AI account and copy your API key from the dashboard.
Add your key as JINA_API_KEY in your environment file.
In a server route, fetch https://r.jina.ai/<the target URL> with an Authorization: Bearer header carrying your key, and read the response back as Markdown.

builder_notes: Keep JINA_API_KEY server-side and call Reader from server code or a background job, not from the browser.
Cache the Markdown you get back instead of re-fetching the same URL on every request, since Reader still spends tokens or throughput per call.
Respect each target site's robots.txt and terms of service; Reader will fetch whatever URL you give it.
